title: Count the Number of Arrays with K Matching Adjacent Elements
summary: Given integers n, m, and k, calculate the count of arrays of size n where each element is between 1 and m, and exactly k consecutive elements are the same.
statement: Given integers n, m, and k, calculate the count of arrays of size n where each element is between 1 and m, and exactly k consecutive elements are the same. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Count arrays having exactly k indices i where values[i] equals values[i+1], modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def count_arrays_with_k_equal_neighbors(n,m,k):
    modulo=1000000007
    def choose(total,take):
        if take<0 or take>total:return 0
        numerator=denominator=1
        for value in range(1,take+1):numerator=numerator*(total-take+value)%modulo;denominator=denominator*value%modulo
        return numerator*pow(denominator,modulo-2,modulo)%modulo
    return choose(n-1,k)*m*pow(m-1,n-k-1,modulo)%modulo

hints: Choose the k matching boundaries; every other boundary must change value.
After choosing the first of m values, each nonmatching boundary has m-1 choices.
Multiply C(n-1,k), m, and (m-1)^(n-k-1) modulo the prime.
Boundary selections and value choices uniquely construct every valid array and never alter the exact match count.

The arrays [1,2] and [2,1] have no equal adjacent pair, so the answer is two.
